recognize_zh: 中央四顆細胞約為紅血球的 1.5–2 倍大，核質比極高，只有一圈很薄的淡藍細胞質，染色質細緻，部分可見小核仁，細胞質無顆粒也無 Auer rod；這種小型均一的母細胞符合急性淋巴性白血病（ALL）。
features: Four small-to-medium blasts, about 1.5–2 times a red cell diameter
Very high N:C ratio with scant rim of pale basophilic cytoplasm
Round nuclei with finely dispersed to slightly condensed chromatin
Small or indistinct nucleoli in some cells
No cytoplasmic granules or Auer rods; background normochromic red cells without other leukocytes
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a small cluster of four blasts that are small to medium in size with a very high N:C ratio and a scant rim of agranular pale basophilic cytoplasm. Nuclei are round with finely dispersed to slightly condensed chromatin and small, inconspicuous nucleoli. Cytoplasmic granules and Auer rods are absent. Background red cells are normochromic, and no maturing granulocytes are seen in this field. Findings are consistent with lymphoblasts suggestive of acute lymphoblastic leukemia; flow cytometry is required to confirm lymphoid lineage (B versus T) and exclude minimally differentiated AML.

ddx.vs: Myeloblasts are usually larger with more cytoplasm, prominent nucleoli and may contain granules or Auer rods; confirm by MPO and flow cytometry.
Hematogones are mainly in marrow of children or regenerating marrow, have homogeneous condensed chromatin, and show a normal maturation spectrum on flow cytometry.

ddx.dx: Leukemic phase of mature lymphoma (e.g., mantle cell, CLL)
ddx.vs: Mature lymphoma cells have more condensed chromatin, possible nuclear clefts and smudge cells, and are TdT/CD34-negative.
Burkitt cells have deeply basophilic cytoplasm with prominent lipid vacuoles and multiple nucleoli.
